title: The naive cotangent complex of a symmetric algebra is the image of K tensor C; its differentials are M tensor C
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $0\to K\to A^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{\ \pi\ }M\to0$ an exact sequence of $A$-modules; write $e_1,\dots,e_m$ for the standard basis of $A^{\oplus m}$, $m_j=\pi(e_j)$, and for $k=\sum_jk_je_j\in K$ put $\ell(k)=\sum_jk_jy_j\in P:=A[y_1,\dots,y_m]$. Let $C=\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$ with $\iota_M:M\to C$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property], let $\alpha:P\to C$ be the homomorphism of $A$-algebras with $\alpha(y_j)=\iota_M(m_j)$, and $J=\ker\alpha$. Then: (1) $\alpha$ is surjective and $J$ is the ideal of $P$ generated by the linear forms $\ell(k)$, $k\in K$; (2) the $C$-linear map $\lambda:K\otimes_AC\to J/J^2$, $k\otimes c\mapsto c\cdot(\ell(k)\bmod J^2)$, is well defined and surjective; (3) under the basis $\mathrm dy_1,\dots,\mathrm dy_m$ of $\Omega_{P/A}$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], the composite of $\lambda$ with the map $\delta:J/J^2\to C\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A}=\bigoplus_{j=1}^mC\,\mathrm dy_j$, $u\bmod J^2\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm du$, of the naive cotangent complex of the presentation $\alpha$ is $k\otimes c\mapsto\sum_jck_j\,\mathrm dy_j$, and $\operatorname{im}\delta=\operatorname{im}(\delta\circ\lambda)$; (4) $\Omega_{C/A}\cong M\otimes_AC$ as $C$-modules, by the isomorphism sending $\mathrm d(\iota_M(x))$ to $x\otimes1$ for $x\in M$ ($\Omega$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]). (The map $\lambda$ is not injective in general, contrary to the first assertion of Stacks 07EV: for $A=\mathbb Z$, $M=(\mathbb Z/p)^{\oplus2}$, $K=p\mathbb Z^{\oplus2}$, the nonzero element $pe_1\otimes\iota_M(m_2)-pe_2\otimes\iota_M(m_1)$ of $K\otimes_AC$ is sent to the class of $py_1y_2-py_2y_1=0$.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07EV (lemma-cotangent-complex-symmetric-algebra, line 2067) and its proof (lines 2081-2107, via Algebra Lemma Tag 00DO, lemma-presentation-sym-exterior, algebra.tex line 2241); the 'in particular' $\Omega_{C/A}=M\otimes_AC$ is what Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CE (smoothing.tex line 374) and [lem-weil-pbc-improve-presentation] use. The first assertion of 07EV ($J/J^2\cong K\otimes_AC$) is false in general (counterexample in the statement); the node states the true part: surjectivity of $K\otimes_AC\to J/J^2$ and the consequences for $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)$ and $\Omega_{C/A}$.

proof.text: ($\alpha$ is surjective and $J=(\ell(k):k\in K)$.) The $m_j$ generate $M$ since $\pi$ is surjective, so $\iota_M(m_1),\dots,\iota_M(m_m)$ generate $C$ as an $A$-algebra [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-presentation](a), i.e. $\alpha$ is surjective. Put $F=A^{\oplus m}$ and let $\varphi:\operatorname{Sym}_A(F)\to P$ be the $A$-algebra isomorphism with $\varphi(\iota_F(e_j))=y_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial]; by $A$-linearity of $\iota_F$, $\varphi(\iota_F(k))=\ell(k)$ for $k\in K$. Let $\operatorname{Sym}(\pi):\operatorname{Sym}_A(F)\to C$ be the $A$-algebra map with $\iota_F(x)\mapsto\iota_M(\pi(x))$; its kernel is the ideal generated by $\iota_F(K)$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-quotient-module] (this is Algebra 00DO summed over the degrees). The $A$-algebra maps $\alpha\circ\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Sym}(\pi)$ agree on $\iota_F(e_j)$ (both give $\iota_M(m_j)$), hence on $\iota_F(F)$ by linearity, hence are equal by the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. So $J=\ker\alpha=\varphi(\ker\operatorname{Sym}(\pi))$ is the ideal generated by $\varphi(\iota_F(K))=\{\ell(k):k\in K\}$ (a ring isomorphism carries the ideal generated by a set onto the ideal generated by its image).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00DO (lemma-presentation-sym-exterior, line 2241), summed over all degrees as in More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07EV (more-algebra.tex lines 2086-2090)

proof.text: ($\lambda$ well defined and surjective.) $\ell:K\to J$ is $A$-linear (step 1 shows $\ell(K)\subseteq J$; directly, $\alpha(\ell(k))=\sum_jk_j\iota_M(m_j)=\iota_M(\pi(k))=0$). $J/J^2$ is a $C=P/J$-module, and its $A$-module structure through $A\to C$ is the one from $A\to P$; so the $A$-linear map $K\to J/J^2$, $k\mapsto\ell(k)\bmod J^2$, extends uniquely to a $C$-linear map $\lambda:C\otimes_AK\cong K\otimes_AC\to J/J^2$ with $k\otimes c\mapsto c\cdot(\ell(k)\bmod J^2)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property]. Surjectivity: by step 1 every $u\in J$ is a finite sum $\sum_ip_i\ell(k_i)$ with $p_i\in P$, $k_i\in K$, and in the $C$-module $J/J^2$ one has $p_i\ell(k_i)\bmod J^2=\alpha(p_i)\cdot(\ell(k_i)\bmod J^2)$; so $u\bmod J^2=\lambda(\sum_ik_i\otimes\alpha(p_i))$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07EV (line 2067), proof lines 2081-2090 (J generated in degree 1 by the image of K); the surjectivity argument is written out by the agent

proof.text: (The naive cotangent complex.) By [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] (with $A\to B$ the map $A\to P$ and $\mathfrak a=J$, $C=P/J$ via $\alpha$) the map $\delta:J/J^2\to C\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A}$, $u\bmod J^2\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm du$, is well defined, $P$-linear and hence $C$-linear. $\Omega_{P/A}$ is free on $\mathrm dy_1,\dots,\mathrm dy_m$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], so $C\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A}$ is free over $C$ on $1\otimes\mathrm dy_j$, written $\mathrm dy_j$ (tensor product commutes with finite direct sums and $C\otimes_PP=C$). Since $\mathrm d$ is $A$-linear, $\mathrm d\ell(k)=\sum_jk_j\,\mathrm dy_j$ for $k=\sum_jk_je_j\in K$; hence $\delta(\lambda(k\otimes c))=c\cdot\delta(\ell(k)\bmod J^2)=\sum_jck_j\,\mathrm dy_j$ (with $k_j$ acting through $A\to C$). As $\lambda$ is surjective (step 2), $\operatorname{im}\delta=\operatorname{im}(\delta\circ\lambda)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07EV (line 2067), statement: NL(alpha) = (K tensor C -> sum C dy_j)

proof.text: ($\Omega_{C/A}\cong M\otimes_AC$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] the map $w:C\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A}\to\Omega_{C/A}$, $c\otimes\mathrm dp\mapsto c\,\mathrm d\alpha(p)$, is surjective with kernel $\operatorname{im}\delta$, which by step 3 is $\operatorname{im}(\delta\circ\lambda)$. Identify $\bigoplus_jC\,\mathrm dy_j$ with $F\otimes_AC$ by $c\,\mathrm dy_j\leftrightarrow e_j\otimes c$; by step 3, $\delta\circ\lambda$ becomes $i\otimes\mathrm{id}_C$ for the inclusion $i:K\to F$. Tensoring the exact sequence $K\to F\xrightarrow{\pi}M\to0$ with $C$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], so $\pi\otimes\mathrm{id}_C:F\otimes_AC\to M\otimes_AC$ is surjective with kernel $\operatorname{im}(i\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)$. Two surjective $C$-linear maps out of $F\otimes_AC$ with the same kernel induce a $C$-linear isomorphism $\Omega_{C/A}\cong M\otimes_AC$, sending $w(\mathrm dy_j)=\mathrm d\iota_M(m_j)$ to $m_j\otimes1$. For $x=\sum_ja_jm_j\in M$ ($a_j\in A$) we get $\mathrm d\iota_M(x)=\sum_ja_j\,\mathrm d\iota_M(m_j)\mapsto\sum_ja_jm_j\otimes1=x\otimes1$, by $A$-linearity of $\iota_M$ and $\mathrm d$.

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED (first assertion of the old statement and of Stacks 07EV): the map K tensor_A C -> J/J^2 is surjective but not injective in general. Counterexample: A=Z, M=(Z/p)^2, K=pZ^2, C=Sym_Z(M); x=pe_1 tensor iota(m_2) - pe_2 tensor iota(m_1) is nonzero in K tensor C_1 = (pZ tensor F_p)^4 = F_p^4 but maps to py_1y_2-py_2y_1=0 (in degree 2, (J/J^2)_2 = pSym^2/p^2Sym^2 = F_p^3 while (K tensor C)_2 = F_p^4). Stacks' proof errs where it takes J_d/(J^2)_d as a cokernel of K tensor K tensor Sym^{d-2} -> K tensor Sym^{d-1}, ignoring the kernel of K tensor Sym^{d-1}(A^m) -> Sym^d(A^m). The statement is corrected to what is true and what the citers use: (1) alpha surjective, J generated by the linear forms from K; (2) lambda surjective; (3) the NL map composed with lambda is (Sum k_j e_j) tensor c -> Sum c k_j dy_j with the same image; (4) Omega_{C/A} = M tensor C. The only citer, lem-weil-pbc-improve-presentation (step 4), uses only (4), so it is unaffected; Stacks 07CE's display (equation-sequence) uses J/J^2 = K tensor C but only after localizing where M and K are projective. Proof in 4 steps from existing nodes (all in unit sk-thm-p1): symmetric-algebra finite-presentation (a), free-module-polynomial, quotient-module (Algebra 00DO), universal property, module base change, jacobi-zariski-differential-maps (Mathlib leaf), polynomial Kähler basis, tensor right exact. No new nodes.
